card.keepWhy: The scales fell. He could see.
sources: Acts 9:1-2 (Saul, breathing threats, asks the high priest for letters to the synagogues of Damascus to bring followers of the Way bound to Jerusalem)
Acts 9:3-4 (near Damascus a light from heaven flashed around him; he fell to the earth; “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”)
Acts 9:5 (“Who are you, Lord?” “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting”)
Acts 9:7 (his companions heard the voice but saw no one)
Acts 9:8-9 (he could see no one; led by the hand into Damascus; three days without sight, neither ate nor drank)
Acts 9:10-14 (Ananias in a vision; “I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints”)
Acts 9:17-18 (“Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road… has sent me”; something like scales fell from his eyes; he was baptized)
Acts 9:11 (the street called Straight), behind painting SC5 only
Acts 13:9 (“Saul, who is also called Paul”); the caption’s “wrote letters” gives no number (13 letters bear his name; scholars agree on at least seven)
Psalm 119:18 (“Open my eyes, that I may see”), used in the today step
check: Painting SC5 shows a few glinting flakes falling from Saul’s eyes; the text says only “something like scales.” Confirm the picture is acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever been totally sure about something, or someone, and then found out you were wrong?
options: that takes courage to admit. this story is for you.
i get it. listen to what happened to the surest man around.
fair. this one might change how you see someone.

steps.line: Saul was a brilliant, fierce young man. He hunted the first followers of Jesus, and set off for Damascus with letters to arrest more.
steps.label: Acts 9:1-2

steps.line: Near the city, a light from heaven flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
steps.label: Acts 9:3-4

steps.line: “Who are you, Lord?” “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.”
steps.label: Acts 9:5

steps.q: Saul was hunting Jesus’s followers, not Jesus himself. So why does the voice say, “Why are you persecuting me?”
o: Because hurting his followers was hurting Jesus himself
Because Saul had once arrested Jesus in person
Because the voice was speaking to everyone on the road
steps.why: Christians take this deeply: Jesus counts his people as his own body. What you do to them, you do to him.

steps.q: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.” What do you think the voice tells Saul to do?
o: Go home and stop hunting them
Go into the city and wait
Find the believers and beg forgiveness
steps.why: “Get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do” (Acts 9:6). No plan, no explanation. And when he stands up, he can’t see.

steps.line: Saul got up, but he couldn’t see. His companions led him by the hand into Damascus. For three days he didn’t eat or drink.
steps.label: Acts 9:8-9

steps.line: In a vision, the Lord told a believer named Ananias to go to Saul. Ananias was afraid. “I’ve heard how much harm this man has done.” But he went.
steps.label: Acts 9:10-17

steps.q: When Ananias objects, the Lord answers with a surprising description of Saul. What?
steps.why: Acts 9:15: chosen to carry Jesus’s name to the Gentiles, to kings and to Israel. The hunter is about to become one of the most traveled messengers of the faith.

steps.pre: Ananias walked in, laid his hands on the man he feared, and said, “
steps.post: Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me.”
steps.why: “Brother.” Not “enemy,” not “sir.” Hold onto that word.

steps.line: Ananias laid his hands on him. “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me.” Something like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see.
steps.label: Acts 9:17-18

steps.line: Saul was baptized. The man who hunted Jesus’s followers became one of them. Saul, also called Paul, wrote letters you can still read in the Bible.

steps.q: Many people think Saul was renamed Paul on the road to Damascus. What does Acts actually say?
o: Jesus gave him the name on the road
Ananias renamed him at his baptism
He had both; Paul was his Roman name
steps.why: Acts never tells of a renaming. It just says “Saul, who is also called Paul” (13:9), and uses Paul once he works among non-Jews.

say: here’s what i love. God didn’t only change saul. he sent a frightened man to call him brother.
christians read this as conversion: a whole new way of seeing. the surest man on the road learned he’d been the one who couldn’t see.

steps.q: Saul could see fine before the light, and was blind after. Christians often say it was really the other way round. How?
o: The light was a punishment that lasted three days
Before, he was blind to who Jesus was. After, he saw
Ananias healed an eye sickness Saul already had
steps.why: His eyes were fine, but he couldn’t see the truth. Three dark days later, he saw both.

today.say: pick one person you’ve already made up your mind about. this week, listen to them fully before you answer, the way ananias walked in and said “brother.” if you’d like, pray the old psalm line “open my eyes, that i may see”: watch, learn, or join in. your choice.
options: then start there. one honest listen can take the scales off.
good. ananias was scared too, and he still knocked on the door.

tomorrow.title: Joseph forgives.
tomorrow.line: his brothers sold him. years later, they bowed before him and didn’t know his face.
